subject: Next steps: deployment mode, SLO targets, and procurement path
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Sam Green <sam.green@pioneer-analytics.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + ask: deployment mode, latency SLO, procurement owner

Thanks for the time this morning, Sam — good conversation. Quick recap + concrete asks so we can map the procurement path and get you a tailored estimate: 

1) Decision criteria we heard:
- Required data residency / control: looks like private deployment (VPC / on‑prem) is preferred because of PHI handling.
- Latency target: you mentioned p95 goals for typical 512-token queries; please confirm numeric target (we have proposals at 150ms, 200ms, 300ms).
- Cost sensitivity: mid‑range; economic buyer will want cost per 1M tokens + committed capacity pricing.

2) Asks / owners:
- Can you confirm the economic buyer and procurement timeline? (Who signs contracts/POs) — Sam
- Security contact who will own the questionnaire / SOC2 evidence — Sam said James Liu, please confirm.
- Preferred deployment mode (Hosted API vs Redwood Dedicated vs Private VPC/on‑prem). We should confirm whether a short Dedicated trial would be acceptable while procurement completes. — Ben / Karthik to advise.

3) Next meeting: propose 1) security kickoff with James + our security engineer, and 2) internal billing/procurement sync (we can host both next week).

Attachments we'll prepare: initial cost estimate, SLA options matrix, procurement checklist.

Thanks — I’ll draft owners once I have the confirmation on names and timeline.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Attachment: pioneer-procurement-intake.docx (stub)

From: Sam Green <sam.green@pioneer-analytics.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Nora Patel <nora.patel@pioneer-analytics.com>, James Liu <james.liu@pioneer-analytics.com>, procurement@pioneer-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + ask: deployment mode, latency SLO, procurement owner

Thanks Lauren — appreciate the clear summary. Confirmations below: 

- Economic buyer: Nora Patel (CPO). I’ve looped her in. Final signoff goes through her team; procurement will issue a PO once commercial terms are agreed.
- Security owner: James Liu (copied). He will own the questionnaire and prefers to start with a short security kickoff; he asked for our standard SOC2 + network architecture.
- Deployment preference: Private VPC is their preference due to PHI and internal policy. However, they are open to a short Dedicated pool trial for evaluation if it helps validate latency.
- Latency target: Target p95 <= 200ms for 512-token median workloads (this is what the product team has prioritized). If you can show numbers at 150ms that will be a differentiator, but 200ms is workable.
- Procurement timeline: 6–8 weeks from SOW acceptance (internal approvals + legal review). Procurement intake form attached.

Attached: Pioneer_Procurement_Intake.docx (filled) — includes billing contact and internal PO workflow.

Sam
Sam Green
Director, Product Engineering
Pioneer Analytics
sam.green@pioneer-analytics.com
Attachment: Pioneer_Procurement_Intake.docx (stub)

Quick: this is good. Notes from sales ops perspective — copying Karthik to own the technical estimate: 

- If Pioneer wants Private VPC, we should prepare two commercial scenarios: 1) Private (on‑prem/VPC) with 1‑year commitment; 2) Dedicated trial (4 weeks) leading into Private. Pricing and SLA differ materially.
- I'll draft an "initial-cost-estimate.pdf" with both rows and include committed capacity pricing and burst policies.
- Recommend we surface SLA tiers aligned to p95 targets (150ms = enterprise tier with higher commitment; 200ms = standard enterprise tier). I’ll attach the draft.

Action: Karthik — can you prepare a latency validation plan (test harness + expected tokens/seq len) and confirm whether our KV cache + batching approach meets 200ms p95 under the expected profile?

Ben

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + ask: deployment mode, latency SLO, procurement owner — next steps and owners

Great — thanks Sam and team. Finalizing owners and next steps here so everyone has a single source of truth: 

1) Security kickoff (owner: James Liu / Redwood sec lead: Karthik Iyer)
   - Proposed slot: Wed Dec 2, 10:00–10:45 PT. Karthik will bring architecture notes and SOC2 artifacts.
2) Latency validation plan (owner: Karthik Iyer)
   - Deliverable: test harness, expected p95 numbers vs. 512-token profile, instrumentation for KV cache metrics — ETA Tue Dec 6.
3) Commercial scenario + initial estimate (owner: Ben Carter)
   - Deliverable: two scenarios (Private 1yr commit / Dedicated 4wk trial -> Private) + SLA tiers mapped to p95 targets; Ben to share draft by Tue Dec 6.
4) Procurement & contracting (owner: Lauren Bishop)
   - I will prepare a SOW + DocuSign template for standard terms; target to have an initial SOW ready for review by Fri Dec 10.
5) Next meeting: Security kickoff (above) + follow-up commercial review after validation results.

Attachments: redwood-sla-table.xlsx (SLA tiers + metrics), procurement-checklist.pdf (procurement intake checklist), initial-cost-estimate.pdf (draft).

Links: HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.example.com/deal/1198) — please add any procurement docs there.

If this matches your expectation, Sam / Nora, confirm the security kickoff slot and we’ll book.

Best,
